title: Eval Cup leaderboard with a contest window
scenario: Keep each active team's best result per active benchmark inside an end-exclusive contest window, normalise against the benchmark leader into a weighted composite, and rank with an earliest-finisher tie-break. The report counts distinct entrants per benchmark.

verified.why_correct: It tries exactly the three formats the README lists, with month/day order for the slash format, and raises on anything else. The `continue` inside `except` only moves on to the next format.
For a lower-is-better benchmark the leader has the smallest value, so `best / score` puts the leader at 1.0 and every slower team below 1. It looks inverted, but it is exactly spec rule 6.

bugs.title: Submission at the window end counted
bugs.symptom: test_1_mid_table_composites fails: orca shows (0.7167, 52.0) instead of (0.7, 48.0). puffin and otter are unchanged and the standings test still passes.
bugs.why: The window is end-exclusive. With `<=`, orca's S24 (exactly 2026-09-15 00:00, written as 09/15/2026 00:00) counts, so orca's reasoning best rises from 48 to 52 and its composite from 0.7 to 0.7167. It is not enough to change orca's rank.
hints: orca's reasoning best is 52. Which submission is that, and when was it made?
Compare that time with contest.json and the window rule in the README.
probes: Why did the standings test still pass with this bug?
S35 is exactly at `start`. Why must it stay in?

bugs.title: Tie-break uses first submission time
bugs.old: last_seen = {team: max(ts) for team, ts in times.items()}
bugs.new: last_seen = {team: min(ts) for team, ts in times.items()}
bugs.symptom: test_2_final_standings fails: heron is ranked 6th and lynx 7th. Expected lynx then heron (both have composite 0.6667).
bugs.why: lynx and heron have identical bests and composites (0.6667). The tie goes to whoever made their last submission earlier (lynx, 09-10 vs heron 09-12). `min` gives each team's first submission instead, and heron started earlier (09-02), so the two swap.
hints: Which two teams swapped places? Compare their composites.
The sort key in ranking.py looks right. Where do its time values come from?
team_bests builds last_seen with min(ts); rule 9 needs max(ts).
probes: Why is ranking.py, the file that does the sorting, not where the fix goes?
Why can't the team id ever decide the order in this data?

bugs.title: Entrant count counts submissions, not teams
bugs.symptom: test_3_benchmark_stats fails: latency_ms teams is 8 (expected 7) and reasoning teams is 9 (expected 8). coding and safety are right.
bugs.why: `teams` must count distinct teams. A list keeps one entry per submission, so kelp's two reasoning and two latency submissions are counted twice. coding and safety happen to be right because nobody submitted to them twice.
hints: reasoning and latency_ms are one too high; coding and safety are fine. What is different about those two benchmarks?
Look at how benchmark_stats gathers entrants.
Collect teams in a set (defaultdict(set) / .add) so each team counts once.
probes: Narwhal's S07 appears twice in the CSV. Why didn't it inflate the count too?
Why do coding and safety come out right even with this bug?

context_qa.a: Rows with a blank score, rows whose submission id was already seen (the id is added to `seen` before the window check), and rows outside the window according to `in_window`. Team and benchmark ids are trimmed and lower-cased.

context_qa.q: Where are banned or withdrawn teams removed?
context_qa.a: In `build_leaderboard`: after loading, only submissions whose team maps to status `active` in `load_teams` are kept. A blank status defaults to `active`. Non-active team ids go into `excluded_teams`.

A tuple: a dict team -> {benchmark: best score} using `better()` with the benchmark's direction, and `last_seen`, a dict team -> one datetime built from all of that team's counted submissions on active benchmarks.

context_qa.q: How is the leader of a benchmark picked?
context_qa.a: `benchmark_leaders` walks every team that has a best on that benchmark and keeps the entry that is `better()` than the current one, so it returns (team, score). Benchmarks nobody entered are left out.

context_qa.q: Which benchmarks does composite divide by?
context_qa.a: `total_weight` is the sum of the weights of every active benchmark (6 here), whether or not the team entered it. Missing benchmarks add nothing to `weighted`.
It sorts by `(-composite, last_seen[team], team)` and then writes positions 1..n into `rank`.
